name: Delta Air Lines
description: Delta flies passengers and cargo on a 1,314-aircraft fleet (mainline plus regional partners) and earns most of its money from ticket sales, with a growing share from premium cabins sold to corporate travelers. Two other engines sit alongside the tickets. First, the SkyMiles loyalty program: American Express and other partners buy miles from Delta, and Amex alone paid Delta $8.2B in 2025 (up 11 percent; Delta expects about $10B over the next few years), which is close to pure cash margin and helps carry the airline through downturns. Second, Delta owns the Trainer refinery near Philadelphia (Monroe Energy, about 200,000 barrels of crude a day), which supplies part of its jet fuel and sells the other refined products to third parties ($5.1B of revenue in 2025). Profit is sensitive to fuel prices, demand and unit revenue (TRASM); in the June 2026 quarter revenue jumped 19 percent but operating income fell to $1.86B from $2.10B as fuel and refinery costs surged.

businessLines.name: Passenger (tickets, loyalty awards, travel services)
businessLines.how: Travelers pay per ticket at booking; premium cabins (Delta One, First, Comfort+, Premium Select) earn far more per seat and now bring in nearly as much as main cabin. Miles redeemed for flights are booked as revenue from the loyalty program's deferred balance rather than as new cash. Driven by capacity, load factor (84 percent in 2025), yield and premium mix.
businessLines.description: Main cabin and premium tickets, miles redeemed for flights (loyalty travel awards), and travel-related services (change fees, extras, etc.).

businessLines.name: Loyalty program and American Express co-brand deal
businessLines.how: American Express and other partners pay Delta cash, monthly, for each mile they buy to give to cardholders (Amex remuneration was $8.2B in 2025 and $2.4B in the June 2026 quarter); Delta recognizes the marketing component in other revenue and defers the travel component until miles are redeemed for flights. The card costs Delta little to serve, so this stream is very high margin.
businessLines.description: SkyMiles sells miles to American Express (co-brand credit cards) and other partners (retail, ride sharing, car rental, hotels); part is recognized in 'Loyalty program' other revenue and part flows into passenger revenue as miles are redeemed.

revenue.note: Only the 'Loyalty program' line inside other revenue ($3,362M vs $3,297M); the travel-component of Amex remuneration sits in passenger 'loyalty travel awards' ($4,237M) and is not separable from redemptions. Total Amex remuneration $8.2B in 2025 (cash basis).

businessLines.revenueNote: Only the 'Loyalty program' line inside other revenue ($3,362M vs $3,297M); the travel-component of Amex remuneration sits in passenger 'loyalty travel awards' ($4,237M) and is not separable from redemptions. Total Amex remuneration $8.2B in 2025 (cash basis).

businessLines.name: Refinery (Monroe Energy, Trainer refinery)
businessLines.how: Refines crude into jet fuel (sold to Delta's airline segment, $1,150M in 2025) and other products such as gasoline and diesel sold to third parties ($5,077M in 2025) or exchanged for jet fuel; profit is the refining margin, which is volatile and hedged with derivatives.
businessLines.description: Trainer refinery near Philadelphia (about 200,000 barrels of crude a day) and associated pipelines and terminals; makes jet fuel for Delta and other products for sale.

businessLines.name: Cargo, ancillary businesses and miscellaneous
businessLines.how: Shippers pay per shipment on Delta's flights; airlines pay TechOps per maintenance job; smaller items billed as services.
businessLines.description: Air cargo; Delta TechOps maintenance for other airlines; other ancillary and miscellaneous revenue.
